name: Isolation forest
summary: Flags anomalies as points that random splits isolate quickly; fast and unsupervised.
outputs: Anomaly score per row and a binary flag at a chosen contamination rate.
assumptions: Anomalies are few and different, so they are isolated by fewer random splits
Features are on meaningful scales; axis-parallel splits
math_summary: Builds random trees by picking a random feature and random split value; anomaly score is based on the average path length needed to isolate a point, normalised by the expected path length for n points.
when_to_use: Fast first-pass screening for unusual records
when_not_to_use: Anomalies defined by context or sequence (use residual-based methods)
When you have labels (use supervised models)
pitfalls: Contamination parameter sets the threshold arbitrarily
Weak on high-dimensional data with many irrelevant features

compute.complexity: Linear time, O(n_trees * psi log psi) with sub-sample size psi; low memory.

applicability.use_case: Data-quality screening of statistical releases before modelling
